unaddressed_comments.body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `positionalReadOptions` method is called on every invocation of `readFully` and `readTail`. It retrieves the configured read options, calls `toBuilder()`, sets the file access pattern, and builds a new `GcsReadOptions` instance. In high-throughput big data environments, these methods are on the hot path, and repeated builder instantiation and object allocation creates unnecessary GC pressure.

Since the file system options are immutable for the lifetime of the stream, consider instantiating `positionalReadOptions` once during the construction of `GoogleCloudStorageInputStream` and storing it in a `private final` instance field to avoid redundant allocations.

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. GC Pressure: Avoid allocating large objects or buffers inside tight loops (e.g., in read() loops). Reuse buffers where thread safety allows. <sup>([link](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/gcs-analytics-core/blob/main/.gemini/styleguide.md))</sup>
2. For frequently called methods (hot paths) that require a default or fallback object, reuse a static final constant instance instead of instantiating a new object or builder on every call to avoid redundant allocations and CPU overhead.
</details>
